# Docent

**AI support agent over documentation — RAG, tools, evals.** It answers questions with citations, decides which tools to call, and every change is measured by an evaluation suite.

Built with Claude Code as a coding agent: I design the architecture, review every change and own the result.

The knowledge base is the [FastAPI documentation](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/tree/master/docs/en/docs) (MIT, see `corpus/fastapi/LICENSE`).

**Status:** day 5 of 7 — an agent decides which tools to call (search, read a page, hand off to a person); answers are generated by Claude with citations.

| Part | Status |
|---|---|
| Ingestion: markdown → chunks with heading paths → embeddings → Postgres + pgvector | ✅ |
| Vector search `/search` | ✅ |
| Streaming chat API `/chat` (Server-Sent Events: agent steps, sources, tokens) | ✅ |
| React UI: streaming chat with sources, retrieval panel | ✅ |
| Hybrid search (pgvector + full-text, RRF) — built and measured; not used, vector search scored higher | ✅ |
| Answers with citations (Claude), refusal when the docs don't cover it | ✅ |
| Agent with tools: search, read page, hand-off to a human; step budget, error recovery, traces | ✅ |
| Evaluation: golden set + retrieval metrics (hit@k, MRR) ✅; agent vs plain RAG (evidence, hand-offs, steps, latency) ✅; LLM-as-judge for answers ⏳ | 🟡 |

## Run

```bash
docker compose up -d                      # Postgres 16 + pgvector on :5435
cd backend
python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python -m app.ingest            # ~6 min on CPU: 156 pages → ~2400 chunks
.venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --reload   # http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests

cd ../frontend && npm install && npm run dev   # http://localhost:5173, /api is proxied to :8000
```

## Decisions

- **Chunks keep their heading path** ("Security › OAuth2 › Scopes"): it is embedded together with the text and shown as the citation.
- **Embeddings:** `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` via fastembed (ONNX, CPU, 384 dims) — free, local, good enough for an English corpus; queries get the BGE search instruction, passages don't.
- **Index:** HNSW on cosine distance + a generated `tsvector` column (GIN) for full-text search.
- **Hybrid search was built and rejected by the numbers.** `hybrid_search` merges vector and full-text results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (ranks only, so cosine and `ts_rank` never need one scale). On the golden set it was worse than vector search alone, even on questions with exact code names — the embedding model handles identifiers like `GZipMiddleware` well. Chat stays on vector search; the hybrid code stays for a corpus where it pays off (error codes, SKUs).
- **Streaming:** `/chat` sends Server-Sent Events (`sources` → `token`… → `done`). The UI reads them with a custom `useChatStream` hook (`fetch` + `ReadableStream`, cancellation through `AbortController`), so swapping the extractive answer for an LLM later does not touch the UI.
- **UI state:** chat history in `useReducer`, server state (retrieval panel) in TanStack Query with deferred input, shared settings in a memoised Context.
- **Generation backends** (`backend/app/llm.py`): the Anthropic SDK when `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is set (streaming, cached system prompt, server-side refusal fallback), the local `claude -p` CLI for development, or extractive answers with no model — so a fresh clone runs without credentials. Picked by `LLM_BACKEND` (`auto` by default).
- **Prompt:** numbered `<source>` blocks, every claim cited as `[n]`, "not covered" instead of answering from memory, and sources treated as data, not instructions (a guard against prompt injection through documents).
- **Agent loop is hand-written** (`backend/app/agent.py`), not a framework: a hard step budget, tool errors returned to the model as observations (unknown tool, bad input, a crashing tool), and a trace of every step stored in `traces` for evals. Hand-offs open a row in `tickets`.
- **The agent only gathers evidence; the cited answer is a separate step.** This lets the evaluation measure the tool decisions and the answer quality separately, and `mode: "rag"` (one search, no agent) stays as the baseline.
- **Planners behind one interface:** native tool use via the Anthropic SDK; a JSON-reply protocol for a model without a tools API (the local `claude -p`); and a no-model "search once" planner. The loop is unit-tested with a scripted planner — no database or LLM needed.

## Evaluation

Golden set: `evals/golden.jsonl` — 30 questions phrased the way users ask (not the page titles), 6 "keyword" questions with exact code names (`TrustedHostMiddleware`, `response_model_exclude_unset`), each with the page(s) that answer it, plus 5 out-of-scope questions the agent should hand off. Run `python -m app.evals` in `backend/`.

**Retrieval, vector search, k = 6** (first run, 2026-11-04):

| Variant | hit@6 | hit@1 | MRR | distinct pages in top 6 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Vector search | 0.933 | 0.667 | 0.754 | 3.3 |
| + max 2 chunks per page | 0.933 | 0.667 | 0.754 | 4.3 |
| + release notes excluded | 0.933 | 0.667 | 0.771 | 3.2 |

**Vector vs full-text vs hybrid, k = 6** (2026-11-05; MRR, natural questions / keyword questions):

| Search | hit@6 natural | MRR natural | hit@6 keyword | MRR keyword |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Vector** (used) | **0.933** | **0.754** | **1.0** | **0.917** |
| Full-text (OR of stemmed terms, `ts_rank_cd`) | 0.567 | 0.353 | 1.0 | 0.889 |
| Hybrid, RRF, equal weights | 0.867 | 0.617 | 1.0 | 0.875 |
| Hybrid, RRF, full-text weight 0.3 | 0.867 | 0.775 | 0.833 | 0.75 |

Full-text matching on everyday wording pulls in pages that share common words (often the release notes), and fusion carries that noise into the top 6. Down-weighting full-text recovers MRR on natural questions but loses a keyword question — and a weight tuned on 30 questions would be tuned to this set, so I did not ship it.

**Agent vs plain RAG** (`python -m app.agent_evals --planner …`, 2026-11-05, 36 documented + 5 out-of-scope questions; per-question results in `evals/runs/`):

| | Evidence has the right page | Hand-off precision / recall | Avg tool calls | p50 / p90 latency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain RAG (one search with the question) | 0.944 | — / 0.0 | 1.0 | 0.07 s / 0.13 s |
| **Agent** (Claude Sonnet via `claude -p`) | **0.972** | **1.0 / 1.0** | 1.37 | 14 s / 36 s |

- The agent fixes the CORS miss by rewriting the query ("CORS cross origin localhost React…"), and it hands off all 5 out-of-scope questions (refund, Django, "a real person", account deletion, weather) without touching a documented one. Plain RAG cannot hand off at all — it would answer the refund question from whatever it found.
- The price is latency: ~200× slower, most of it the CLI starting a process per step. The API planner with prompt caching is the next thing to measure.
- Remaining miss: "apply an API key check to every route" — the agent searched three times and found a page that only *links* to global dependencies.
- **A bug the eval caught:** in the first run 6 of 41 questions had a broken step. The text-only model wrote its tool call and then kept going, inventing the tool's "Result:" itself; the parser took everything up to the last brace and failed. Now only the first JSON object is parsed and the transcript stores the parsed call, never the raw reply, so an invented result cannot become evidence (regression test in `tests/test_agent.py`).

What the misses show:
- *"My React app on localhost:3000 gets blocked…"* never says "CORS", and pure vector search does not find the CORS page. The agent rewrites the query to "CORS…" and finds it — the case the agent exists for (the agent eval will measure it).
- The release notes mention every feature and crowd real pages out of the results.
- Hybrid search does not fix the CORS miss either: the question shares no words with the page.
- Next: LLM-as-judge for the answers themselves (correct, grounded, cited) — tool choice, hand-off accuracy, steps, latency — against the plain-RAG baseline.
